title: Frontend: Worker Pool
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Worker Pool. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({workers,jobs,events}), the dispatcher core of a worker pool. Jobs are unique IDs queued initially; worker IDs are 0..workers-1. Initially assign in queue order to idle workers ascending. done{worker} records its active job; crash{worker} retries that active job at queue front, then replaces the worker. Ignore events for idle workers. Return {assignments,completed,active,queued}; assignments are [worker,job]. This tests the protocol reducer, not actual CPU parallelism.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
A promise concurrency loop does not create CPU parallelism.
alternativeApproaches: Add backpressure, per-task deadlines, and worker replacement without leaking unsettled promises.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Worker crash; timeout; out-of-order results.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
